subject: Reserved node outage: RCA summary, temporary mitigations, and customer action items
messages:
From: Redwood Support <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Urgent] Reserved nodes experiencing degraded capacity — initial update

Hi Sara,

We’re seeing elevated queuing and timeouts on your reserved GPU pool in us-west-2 starting around 08:45 PDT this morning. Our runtime detected sustained node saturation on the pool backing your reserved capacity which caused autoscale attempts to fail and a subset of requests to fall back to lower-throughput paths.

What we’ve done so far:
- Scoped the impacted pool (pool-id: rsv-usw2-14).
- Initiated emergency scale-up of warm placeholders.
- Routed high-priority traffic to a nearby failover pool to keep critical requests moving.

Immediate visible impact: 10–25% increased tail latency for generation requests, and sporadic 5–10% request failures for large-context workloads. No data exfiltration.

We’re investigating root cause and will send a corrective plan within 2 hours. Please confirm if you’d like us to route all traffic to the failover pool for the next 24 hours (this will increase per-token cost slightly).

Attachments: cluster-logs-2026-08-07.tar.gz (log archive)

Sorry for the disruption — we know this affects your production flows. I’ll follow up with a concrete mitigation and timeline shortly.

— Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acmeretail.com>
To: Redwood Support <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:35:22 -0700
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Reserved nodes experiencing degraded capacity — initial update

Thanks Karthik —

Please route all traffic to the failover pool for now. Our checkout pipeline is most sensitive to latency this morning (promo launch). Also cc’ing ops@acmeretail.com — if you can share an ETA on when normal capacity will return that’d be great.

Sara
VP, Engineering — Acme Retail
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 10:01:13 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved node saturation — triage notes and temporary runbook

Team — quick notes from the triage call: 

- Symptom: sustained >95% GPU utilization on a subset of nodes + slow kernel allocation leading to failed autoscale spikes. Observed repeated kernel OOMs on quantized variants when sequence lengths >6k tokens.
- Probable contributing factors: (a) a regression in kernel selection logic that elected a slower kernel under high memory pressure, (b) an unlucky concentration of long-context demo jobs from a couple of customers during the promo.

Immediate mitigations applied (done):
- Forced fallback to pre-warmed high-memory instances for affected requests.
- Disabled the new heuristic in kernel-selector (reverted commit 1a2b3c).
- Applied targeted throttling on background batch jobs for non-critical tenants.

Next actions (owners):
- Diego: collect full perf counters and upload to support drive (ETA 2h).
- Monica: draft customer-facing mitigation note with cost/impact (ETA 90m).
- Karthik: confirm routing change with Acme and capture permission for temporary failover (in flight).

I’m attaching the quick mitigation runbook.

—Evelyn
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime

Attachments: mitigation-runbook-20260807.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acmeretail.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved node outage: RCA summary, temporary mitigations, and customer action items

Sara — thanks for the quick reply and permission to route traffic. We’ve moved your production routes to the failover pool as requested at 11:12 PDT. You should see reduced tail latency within minutes; I’ll keep monitoring and will share a short summary of the tradeoffs below.

What changed for Acme (short):
- Routing: All traffic from your reserved cluster rerouted to failover pool in us-west-2 (higher hourly cost on fallback nodes; per-token charge slightly higher).
- Expected SLA: latency back to normal for interactive workloads; large batched long-context jobs may still observe elevated completion times until kernel fallback is fully stabilized.
- Credits: We’ll apply a one-time usage credit for the increased spend during the failover window. I’ll confirm amount once we have the full hours.

Planned next technical steps: 
1) Diego will complete perf-counter export and we’ll confirm the kernel-selector regression as root cause (target EOD PST).
2) Engineering will deploy a targeted hotfix to the kernel-selector rollback across affected pools (ETA 24h).
3) After hotfix and stabilization, we’ll rotate traffic back to your reserved nodes and run a short canary (2–3 minutes) before full restore.

If you prefer a phone call to walk through this, I’m available at 11:45–12:30 PDT.

— Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acmeretail.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: root cause, timeline, and credits applied

Sara — following up with the post-incident summary after the work over the weekend. Thanks again for your patience and for the quick permission to failover.

Root cause (short): a kernel-selection regression (commit 1a2b3c) under specific memory-pressure patterns caused suboptimal kernel choices for quantized attention on long-context requests. Under heavy concurrent load this produced repeated memory fragmentation and kernel OOMs preventing autoscale from completing.

What we did:
- Reverted the kernel-selector heuristic and rolled the hotfix across the affected us-west-2 pools (completed Sat 03:20 PDT).
- Rebalanced warm placeholders and ran a canary on your reserved nodes (completed Sat 05:15 PDT).
- Restored normal routing and monitored throughput for 48 hours.

Impact and remediation:
- Customer-visible: 2.1 hours of elevated errors and a 6-hour window of degraded tail latency during initial mitigation and stabilization.
- Credits: We’ve applied a one-time credit of $14,800 against your August invoice to offset increased failover spend and error impact (line item posted).
- Long-term fix: kernel-selector refactor is scheduled for Q4 with improved stress-tests and a new canary gate for long-context variants.

Attached: cluster-logs-2026-08-07.tar.gz, mitigation-runbook-20260807.pdf

If you have any questions or want a walkthrough of the RCA with our engineering leads, let us know and we’ll schedule a short session.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
